back: (p,d,q): normal ARIMA orders. (P,D,Q): seasonal AR, seasonal differences and seasonal MA at lag m. m: season length.
AIC = 2k - 2 ln L. BIC = k ln(n) - 2 ln L. k parameters, n points, L likelihood. Lower is better.
BIC punishes extra parameters more (for n above 7), so it prefers smaller models. AIC is better for forecast accuracy.

front: When can you compare AIC values?
back: Only for models fitted on the same data with the same differencing (same d and D).

front: What does the Ljung-Box test check?
back: H0: residuals are white noise. A small p-value means leftover autocorrelation, so the model missed a pattern.
